stories.title: Gemini 4 Argon
stories.reason: Genuinely new frontier model (Gemini 4 Argon) with a real capability jump and public benchmark/pricing data; already huge on HN (1044 pts) so most readers have seen the headline but not the specifics.
key_facts: Output capacity up to 1M tokens per response, up from 64K on prior Gemini models
Sets new SOTA on DeepSWE v1.1, a long-horizon software-engineering benchmark
Ties GPT-6 Astra on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 53 points, 1 point above GPT-6.1 Sol's 52
Pricing: $2/M input, $10/M output tokens during promo (standard $4/$20); cached input gets a 95% discount (~$0.10/M)
Initial rollout limited to 'trusted cyber defenders' via a Fairwind Program ahead of wider developer/enterprise access

stories.title: Livenerf: Has Opus 5.5 been nerfed yet?
stories.reason: A reproducible, open-source methodology for catching silent post-launch model-quality regressions went to the HN front page (862 pts) — benchmark criticism as a running tool, not a one-off complaint.
key_facts: 875 GitHub stars; daily eval of 78 fixed questions (screened from 2,336 candidates) drawn from GPQA Diamond, MMLU-Pro, competition math, run against Claude Opus 5.5 since its Sep 22 launch
Baseline pass rate ~54.7%; minimum detectable degradation is ~7.5 accuracy points over a 10-day window
Runs on the Inspect AI framework via Claude Code headless on a Max subscription, no API key needed
As of Sep 30: 7 of 30 baseline days collected; a synthetic validation run correctly detected an injected -4.2±3.9 point degradation

stories.title: You said no MCP
stories.reason: A concrete, reusable pattern (sandboxed codegen to batch MCP tool calls) for anyone building MCP-based agents, from a coding-agent vendor publicly reversing its own anti-MCP stance; 617 HN points.
key_facts: Earendil's coding agent 'Pi' reversed its public no-MCP stance; Pi v0.99.0 (Sep 29) adds MCP support over stdio and streamable HTTP with OAuth
New 'Codemode' feature: model-written JavaScript runs in a QuickJS sandbox so the model can call multiple MCP tools programmatically/in parallel instead of one tool-call per turn
Also ships lazy tool loading, mid-conversation system messages, and per-tool metadata for variable-reasoning-effort models

stories.title: Launch HN: Magnitude (YC S25) – Self-optimizing inference engine for agents
stories.reason: Running code with reproducible numbers against a real baseline (llama.cpp) for local/open-weight inference — exactly the serving/throughput territory this digest prioritizes.
key_facts: Open-source local inference engine (Apache 2.0) that compiles/tunes kernels per-device instead of shipping precompiled kernels
Claims up to 2x faster than llama.cpp: 92% faster decode on Metal, 19% faster on CUDA; 9% faster prefill on Metal, 23% faster on CUDA; 27% lower memory per agent session
5.8k GitHub stars, 400 forks, 1,060 commits; supports Apple Silicon, NVIDIA, AMD, CPU
Integrates with Pi, OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, or any OpenAI-compatible API

stories.title: STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization
stories.reason: KV-cache/recurrent-state quantization paper with released code and a concrete serving-memory win — survives this week's 'no released code = hard pass' filter for arxiv quant papers.
key_facts: 6-bit STEPQuant achieves over 5x recurrent-state compression and cuts total serving memory by up to 68.7%
Targets delta-rule linear-attention models (Gated DeltaNet / Kimi Delta Attention style); separates where quantization errors matter temporally vs. spatially in the recurrent state
Code released: github.com/Dreamer-Toby/STEPQuant

stories.title: SodaMem/SodaMem
stories.reason: Auditable, deterministic agent memory with published, re-gradable benchmark artifacts and real integrations (Claude Code, Cursor, LangGraph via MCP) — running code beating a paper describing the same idea.
key_facts: Temporal knowledge graph memory layer: facts aren't overwritten, they're marked with validity periods and linked via supersession edges
Zero-LLM-call retrieval (BM25 + optional vector search); same query always returns identical results from the same store
LongMemEval: 92.8% (464/500); LoCoMo: 86.88% (1338/1540) end-to-end QA accuracy, with answers/evidence published for independent re-grading
Apache-2.0, 152 GitHub stars; ships HTTP API, Python library, TypeScript SDK, and an MCP server

stories.title: Better prompt caching for GPT-6
stories.reason: Material, quantifiable cost/latency lever for anyone running repeated-prefix (agentic/multi-turn) workloads against GPT-6, with real monitoring tooling to back it up.
key_facts: Cache discounts apply to shared prefixes reused within a 30-minute window; up to 90% discount on cached input tokens
New Prompt Caching Dashboard shows cache hit rate over time and cached-vs-uncached token composition
OpenAI reports >50% reduction in the share of prompt tokens needing fresh processing, across billions of requests over several months

stories.title: PSSA: A non-transformer language model written from scratch in Rust
stories.reason: A tiny but real from-scratch, non-transformer architecture with code and matched-scale numbers against a transformer baseline — the kind of running-code exploration this digest wants even at small scale.
key_facts: PSSA (Plastic State-Space Architecture): recurrent state-space core, 512-slot episodic memory bank, weights that update during the forward pass, pure Rust, no ML frameworks
At 1.5M params / 12.7M training tokens: held-out perplexity 54.4 vs. 83.8 for a matched transformer baseline; 1,716 tok/s training throughput vs. 415
Reports '12x faster' generation on CPU; GPL-3.0, 86 GitHub stars; authors flag text quality at this scale is poor for both models
